facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 水_七杀 (Water carrying The General). Persona The General (七杀). Definition line: "Pressure that doesn't grant permission, the trial that forges". Keyword Force, charge fierce, poles catalyst Command / friction Harshness. Family function: Order. Cost dimension: pressure that does not ask permission; peace can feel like demotion. Arena: forge, campaign, the weight of command, tempering. Classical portrait: pressure as clarity; the trial that forges; force without permission; peace felt as demotion. Ruled domains: Pressure, Command, Crisis. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 正官.
Element arena: Water (depth, current, tide, rain, spring, flow). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Fire. structural_interaction seed: "Water pressing Fire same-polarity — the extinguishing force that doesn't moderate itself".
- k2_overview: "Your Water moves as the General: force that arrives as tide. You command indirectly, positioning, timing, the pressure of inevitability, and opponents find themselves outflanked by someone who never raised a voice. Strategy is your sword arm. The deep game, played patiently, with the current doing the marching."
- k2_functional: "Your discipline moves like a cold current: quiet, total, and felt only when someone crosses it."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Cool-headed","Unblinking","Deep-striking"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Pressure":"You convert pressure into depth: threats make you quieter and more exact. Beware pressure you keep underwater. Even oceans need to storm occasionally.","Command":"You command by current: framing choices, shaping terrain, letting people arrive at your conclusion. It is masterful and unsettling. Show the hand sometimes. Trust grows where strategy is visible.","Crisis":"In crisis you flow while others freeze: instant rerouting, calm surface, decisive undertow. You will save situations quietly and collect credit never. Log your victories somewhere. Currents deserve historians."}

  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 水_正官 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Clockwork","Composed","Far-sighted"],"friction":["Overcautious","Muted","On rails"]}
- Sibling cell 水_正官 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Every risk gets weighed until it drowns. The checking, the double-checking, the waiting for conditions: your prudence has a thoroughness that outlives most opportunities. Nothing bad happens to you, statistically. The cost is that remarkably little of anything happens, and the ledger never shows it."

Core element Fire, energy element Water. Law: Water tames Fire (水克火: rain ends the blaze). Relative to the core the energy is the tamer, so Water is this core's Order. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Fire core that shows Water on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Water as the Order is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 火_水's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: You go cold rather than say what hurt. Going cold keeps you in charge of the hurt, and silence gives no one a way back in. Remember that you stay in the cold as long as anyone you put there.

value_b.text: When crossed, you go cold instead of loud. Silence feels like control, so you would rather let the cold speak than put the hurt into words. You send a message by going cold, and everyone in reach gets it whether you meant to or not.

value.text: Going cold keeps the upper hand without a word. Since a fight means admitting you were hurt, you would rather go cold than lose the argument. You stay cold long after the fight ends, and it is worth remembering what that costs in closeness.

value.text: Whenever someone crosses you, you go cold on them first. You turn cold rather than show an anger that can be answered, and you take away their only way to fix it. You leave them to guess at a fault you never name.

value.text: You are harder on yourself than anyone has been. You would rather catch a fault first than be told, and you are hard on your work before anyone else can be. You take the blame early and never stay long enough for praise.

value_b.text: You get hard on yourself before anyone else can. You would rather be hard on yourself first than be measured, since a fault found first cannot be used against you. Remember that being hard on yourself this early costs you ever hearing you did well.

value.text: Your own work gets the hardest judge you know. Since pleasure in your work feels like dropping your guard, you stay hard on it rather than enjoy it. You pay for being this hard in rest never taken, because nothing you make gets to count.

value.text: You never let up, on anything or anyone. Since letting up feels like losing, you keep the pressure on rather than call the job done. You cannot feel finished until you let up on the thing you finished, and that is worth keeping in mind.

value_b.text: Not letting up is the only speed you know. Since stopping feels like losing your place, you push past the point the work needs you rather than let up. Remember that the pressure you never let up on is pressure you are under too.

value.text: Letting up is something you refuse the people beside you as well. You would rather share the pressure than let up alone, and you keep them at your pace. Never letting up costs them the evenings you gave up, and only you chose it.
